about: Parameter spec for the PlantGen Blender add-on. Author a full species preset (the same JSON the add-on loads) by setting these fields. Generated from the model; do not edit by hand.
scope: The AI sets these PARAMETERS. The user provides the asset MESHES -- leaf blade shape, flower/petal form, bud/bract/catkin geometry -- and does final tweaking. Sizes are multipliers on those meshes (1.0 = the mesh as modelled), so set relative proportions, not absolute size.
curves: A field of type 'curve' is a small graph over a normalised x (its x_axis says what x means, e.g. base->tip or seedling->mature). Set it to one of the named shapes below as {"shape": "<key>"}; every curve field accepts every shape. Raw {"points": [[x, y], ...]} is a rare escape hatch for a shape none of the names fit.

none.description:
No flowers at all. Stems finish their development and stop, the same plant as any other kind minus its inflorescence - for foliage species, and for the branch a catkin hangs from, which has to be able to mature without turning into an inflorescence itself.

Different from an indeterminate plant with nothing to flower with: those stems never stop, and grow on until the plant runs out of developmental span

solitary.description: One flower at the tip of each stem

raceme.description: Flowers on short pedicels along a continuing tip (foxglove, delphinium)

spike.description: Like a raceme but the flowers sit directly on the stem, no pedicels (plantain, many grasses)

corymb.description: A raceme whose lower pedicels are longer, bringing every flower up to about one level (yarrow)

verticillaster.description: Rings of flowers spaced up the stem, each subtended by a pair of leafy bracts, with bare stem between them - the false whorl of the mint family (dead-nettle, motherwort, mint, salvia). Sets Flowers per Whorl and Bract Size, which are ordinary controls the other flowering kinds can use too. Botanically each ring is two condensed cymes rather than a true whorl; this builds a real ring, which reads the same at mint density

catkin.description:
The stems bear no flowers themselves and hang catkins at their nodes instead - hazel, birch, willow. The one type here that is not something a stem turns into at its tip: a hazel's twigs go on being twigs and carry catkins along their length, on short stalks.

Shape them in the Catkins box below. They are modelled rather than instanced, so they hang under their own weight and need no asset assigned

umbel.description: Every pedicel radiating from one point at the tip, filling a dome right through its centre (allium)

flat_umbel.description: An umbel whose pedicels are solved to land on one plane, so the head reads flat (cow parsley, Orlaya)

panicle.description: A branched raceme: the stem carries branches rather than flowers and does not flower itself, and each branch repeats that until the last one, which flowers (oat, astilbe, yucca). Its depth is Branching Depth below, counted inside the inflorescence and independent of Max Branch Order - so a tree can carry panicles on twigs that are already several branch orders deep

cyme.description: The tip flowers first and stops, and growth carries on from shoots just below it, each repeating the pattern. This is the unstamped form: set Relays per Node and Relay Rotation yourself. The four named cymes below - Scorpioid, Helicoid, Dichasium, Pleiochasium - are this same mechanism with those two numbers already set, and are what you want unless you are after a combination they do not name

scorpioid.description: A zigzag chain: the tip flowers and one shoot below it carries on, alternating sides each time, so the whole spray kinks from side to side in one plane (forget-me-not, comfrey, heliotrope). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 180. How hard it zigzags is Branch Angle in the Branching box - +90 grows straight on with no kink, lower values fork harder every relay

helicoid.description: Like a scorpioid cyme but every relay arises on the same side rather than alternating, so instead of zigzagging the spray coils (Alstroemeria, sundew, many nightshades). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 0 - that single number is the whole difference between this and a scorpioid cyme

dichasium.description: The familiar forked cyme: the spent tip is flanked by two shoots, each of which forks again, doubling every generation (chickweed, campion, most pinks). Sets Relays per Node to 2 and Relay Rotation to 90, so successive forks cross rather than stacking in one plane. Note the count doubles per Branching Depth

pleiochasium.description: Three or more shoots in a whorl below each spent tip, giving a broad umbel-like spray (spurge). Sets Relays per Node to 3 and Relay Rotation to 60. The count multiplies by Relays per Node every Branching Depth, so it grows very fast - three at depth 3 is 27 flowers

fields.label: Name
fields.description: The species/preset name shown in the Library and stamped on each plant made from it.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Unique name used in the code and scripting, can be re-defined in Python sub-classes if needed

fields.label: Phyllotaxis

CUSTOM.label: Custom
CUSTOM.desc: Spiral and whorl set by hand

ALTERNATE.label: Alternate (spiral)
ALTERNATE.desc: One per node on a golden spiral (137.5 deg)

DISTICHOUS.label: Distichous
DISTICHOUS.desc: One per node, alternating 180 deg -- two ranks

OPPOSITE.label: Opposite
OPPOSITE.desc: A pair at each node, stacked up the stem

DECUSSATE.label: Decussate
DECUSSATE.desc: A pair at each node, each turned 90 deg from the last

WHORLED.label: Whorled
WHORLED.desc: Three per node, each whorl turned half a step

fields.description: How this level's branches are arranged round their parent -- sets Spiral, Whorl and Whorl Angle. On the stems level: how the stems are spread round the base

fields.label: Spiral Angle
fields.description: Degrees each node turns round the parent from the last

fields.label: Whorl
fields.description: Branches per node, spaced round the parent. On the stems level: how many stems

fields.label: Whorl Angle
fields.description: Degrees between the members of one whorl. 0 spreads them evenly

fields.label: Slide
fields.description: Slide a node's branches along the stem: + up, - down. A pair's members move apart, the first up and the second down, half an internode apart at 1

fields.label: Slide Variation
fields.description: Random slide per node, added to Slide: some pairs slide up, some down

fields.label: Pitch
fields.description: Degrees the branch leaves its parent at. On the stems level: how far the stems splay from vertical

fields.label: Yaw
fields.description: Degrees the branch turns sideways as it leaves its parent

fields.label: Roll
fields.description: Degrees the branch twists about its own axis as it leaves -- where its own branches start round it

fields.label: Pitch Variation
fields.description: Degrees each stem or branch's Pitch (on the stems level, its Splay) deviates either way, drawn per stem or branch

fields.label: Yaw Variation
fields.description: Degrees each stem or branch's Yaw deviates either way, drawn per stem or branch

fields.label: Roll Variation
fields.description: Degrees each stem or branch's Roll deviates either way, drawn per stem or branch -- where its own leaves and branches start round it

fields.label: Steps
fields.description: Nodes the axis has when fully grown. A flowering axis flowers after them

fields.label: Emergence Delay
fields.description: Growth steps each branch of this level waits after the node it leaves forms before it starts growing (on a stems level: steps after the plant starts). Timing only: the full-grown plant is unchanged -- the plant's season lengthens to fit -- so it shows at earlier Days and in Grow Over Timeline. Map it to stagger branches

fields.label: Growth
fields.description: How much of its Steps each axis of this level builds. A branch at 50% is the lower half of the full one, not a smaller copy (its taper and maps stay put), the last node grown partly, and it still flowers at its cut tip. Map it to vary it per branch

fields.label: Seed
fields.description: This level's own seed, on top of the plant's: changing it redraws only this level's variation (length, width, slide, fork chance, mask survival). 0 follows the plant's seed alone

fields.label: Start Length
fields.description: First internode, as a fraction of the parent's internode where the branch attaches

fields.label: Length / Step
fields.description: Each internode is this times the one before -- below 1 shortens toward the tip

fields.label: Length Variation
fields.description: How much each stem or branch of this level varies in length from its siblings, as a fraction -- drawn once per stem or branch, so its internodes stay evenly stepped (on a flowering stretch, the flower spacing varies node to node)

fields.label: Start Width
fields.description: Base width, as a fraction of the parent's width where the branch attaches

fields.label: Width / Step
fields.description: Each node's width is this times the one before -- below 1 tapers

fields.label: Width Variation
fields.description: How much each stem or branch of this level varies in thickness from its siblings, as a fraction. Drawn once per stem or branch, so no taper goes ragged along its length

fields.label: Cross Section

circular.label: Circular
circular.desc: A round stem, the usual case

square.label: Square
square.desc: Four-sided, diagnostic of the mint family

polygonal.label: Polygonal
polygonal.desc: A regular polygon with a side count you set

flattened.label: Flattened
flattened.desc: Squashed across one axis, like a ribbon or a flattened grass culm

winged.label: Winged
winged.desc: A few deep ridges running the length of the stem

ribbed.label: Ribbed
ribbed.desc: Many shallow ridges, like celery or angelica

fields.description: The shape swept along this level's stems or branches. A botanical trait as much as an artistic one - a square stem says mint family, a triangular one says sedge

fields.label: Sides
fields.description: How many flat sides a Polygonal section has

fields.label: Count
fields.description: How many ridges or points run up the stem

fields.label: Depth
fields.description: How far the ridges stand out from the stem's own radius

fields.label: Flatten
fields.description: How far a Flattened section is squashed. 0 is round, 1 is a ribbon

fields.label: Pitch / Step
fields.description: Degrees the growing tip bends each step

fields.label: Roll / Step
fields.description: Degrees the bend's direction turns each step. With Pitch / Step, a helix

fields.label: Growth Pattern

monopodial.label: Monopodial
monopodial.desc: One apex builds the whole axis; its branches come off its sides

sympodial.label: Sympodial
sympodial.desc: The axis grows in units: each ends (Unit End) and one bud below it carries on -- a zig-zag chain

dichasial.label: Dichasial
dichasial.desc: Each unit ends and two buds carry on: a false fork with the spent tip in every crotch

pleiochasial.label: Pleiochasial
pleiochasial.desc: Each unit ends and a ring of Relays buds carries on

pseudomonopodial_relay.label: Pseudomonopodial (Aligned Relay)
pseudomonopodial_relay.desc: A sympodium whose relay continues in line, the spent tip pushed aside: one straight stem with side-set flowers

dichotomous.label: Dichotomous
dichotomous.desc: The growing tip splits into equal forks

pseudomonopodial_fork.label: Pseudomonopodial (Unequal Fork)
pseudomonopodial_fork.desc: The tip splits unequally: a leader carries on, weaker forks peel off -- a fake trunk

fields.description: How this level's axes carry their growth on: one apex, relays from units that end, or a tip that splits

fields.label: Branches
fields.description: How many continuations a fork splits into

fields.label: Fork Probability
fields.description: Chance, per node, that the growing tip forks there

fields.label: Spread
fields.description: Total degrees between the continuations (forks or relays). On an Aligned Relay, twice how far the spent tip is pushed aside

fields.label: Whorl
fields.description: Degrees each fork / relay generation's plane turns from its parent's (180 zig-zags in one plane)

fields.label: Balance
fields.description: How unequal the fork is: 0 equal; higher keeps the leader straighter and makes the other forks shorter, thinner and wider-splayed

fields.label: Unit Steps
fields.description: Nodes in one unit before it ends and relays. The level's Steps is the whole chain's length

fields.label: Relays
fields.description: Buds that carry on from each spent unit

fields.label: Basal Spread
fields.description: How wide the clump's stems are spaced at ground level

fields.label: Spread Variation
fields.description: How irregularly the stems stand: each stem's foot moves by up to this fraction of the Spread in X and in Y, drawn per stem (0.5: up to half the spread). 0 keeps them on an even ring

fields.label: Inflorescence Kind
fields.description: How the flowers are arranged where a stem finishes

fields.label: Relays per Node
fields.description:
How many shoots a cyme starts below its spent tip. 1 gives a monochasium, a single chain that zigzags or coils depending on Relay Rotation; 2 the familiar forked cyme (dichasium); 3 or more a whorled spray (pleiochasium).

The count multiplies by this every Branching Depth, so 2 at depth 4 is 16 tips and 3 at depth 4 is 81. On a panicle this is instead how many branches each node of the main stem puts out

fields.label: Relay Rotation

endpoints.look: with 1 relay/node, every shoot on the same side: the cyme coils (helicoid)
with 2 relays/node, successive forks cross instead of stacking flat (decussate dichasium)
with 1 relay/node, shoots alternate sides and the spray zigzags in a plane (scorpioid)

fields.description:
How far the relays are turned around the stem from one generation of a cyme to the next.

This one number is what separates the classical cymose forms. With 1 relay per node, 180 puts each successive shoot on the opposite side and the spray zigzags in a plane (scorpioid); 0 puts every shoot on the same side and it coils (helicoid). With 2, 90 makes successive forks cross instead of stacking flat.

Measured in the parent stem's own frame, so the rotations compose down the chain rather than each being measured afresh - which is what makes a helicoid cyme a real coil. Only used by the cymose kinds

fields.label: Branching Depth
fields.description:
Makes the inflorescence COMPOUND. At each place it would have put a flower it puts a whole inflorescence of its own kind instead, this many times over. 0 is simple.

1 turns a raceme into a panicle, an umbel into a compound umbel (carrot, cow parsley), a corymb into a compound corymb (yarrow, elder) and a spike into a compound spike (wheat). 2 gives the triple umbels real cow parsley makes. On a cyme it is instead how many times the tip relays, so a long zigzag chain wants 8 or more.

Independent of the Branching levels, which stay the plant's own vegetative branching - a plant can have several levels of branch under two of inflorescence, and one number cannot say both.

Watch the count: every level multiplies it by Rays (or by Relays per Node on a cyme), and it multiplies again by however many branch tips the plant itself has. Depth 2 on a bushy plant is thousands of flowers

fields.label: Branch Count
fields.description: How many branches the main stem of the inflorescence carries. Separate from Flower Count, which is how many flowers each of those branches ends up with - one number used to serve both, so ten branches of three flowers was not expressible. Only used by Panicle

fields.label: Branch Count Variance
fields.description: Random change to the branch count, as a fraction of it. Drawn per axis, so one primary branch carries more than its neighbour

fields.label: Branch Angle Variance
fields.description: Random change to the angle each branch leaves at, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Nodes Variance
fields.description: Random change to how many nodes each branch carries, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Angle
fields.description: Which way an inflorescence branch (or a cyme relay) leaves the main stem, measured from perpendicular. The single biggest control over whether a panicle reads as open and diffuse or contracted and spike-like. On a cyme it is the zigzag angle: the kink between one relay and the spent tip above it is exactly 90 minus this.

endpoints.look: branch flat down the stem (strongly drooping panicle)
branch straight out sideways: a wide, open, diffuse panicle
branches ascending at a diagonal (default)
branches flat up against the stem: a narrow, contracted, spike-like panicle

fields.label: Branch Nodes
fields.description: Nodes an inflorescence branch lays down before it starts flowering - the bare basal stretch of a panicle branch. Only used by Panicle

fields.label: Branch Spacing
fields.description: Gap between successive branches along the main stem of the inflorescence, relative to an ordinary internode. Separate from Flower Spacing on purpose: a panicle stands its branches well apart while crowding the flowers on them, and one number cannot say both. Only used by Panicle

fields.label: Branch Spacing Variance
fields.description: Random change to the gap between branches, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Length
fields.description: How far apart the nodes of an inflorescence branch sit, and so how long the branch is. Separate from Branch Nodes, which is how many flowers it carries - before this a branch could only be lengthened by making it carry more. Only used by Panicle

fields.label: Branch Length Variance
fields.description: Random change to each branch's length, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Width

endpoints.look: thread-thin branches
clearly finer than the stem they leave (default)
as thick as the stem at that point (the maximum -- a branch is never thicker than what carries it)

fields.description: A branch's thickness where it leaves the main stem, as a fraction of that stem's own thickness there - so 1.0 is exactly as thick as the stem it comes off, and it cannot go above that. Same as Pedicel Width. Its graph is the taper along one branch, base to tip, and shapes only the taper - the base width is this number's to set. Thinner branches also arch further, because bending resists as the fourth power of radius. Only used by Panicle

fields.label: Branch Width Variance
fields.description: Random change to each branch's thickness, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Bend
fields.description: A steady arch along each inflorescence branch, held in the branch's own plane, so it turns WITH the branch rather than heading for the ground. This is shape; Branch Droop is weight.

endpoints.look: a quarter turn arching one way
straight branches
a quarter turn arching the other way over the branch's length

fields.label: Branch Bend Variance
fields.description: Random change to each branch's arch, as a fraction of it

fields.label: Branch Droop
fields.description: How far an inflorescence branch turns out of the way it was aimed, over its whole length, measured against gravity (does not turn with the branch). Distinct from Peduncle Droop, which only bends the stretch below the lowest flower and so cannot touch a branch that carries branches rather than flowers.

endpoints.look: branch hangs straight down (a weeping panicle like Buddleja)
branch holds the angle it was aimed
branch swept up toward vertical (an erect, upswept panicle)

fields.label: Branch Droop Variance
fields.description: Random change to how far each branch turns, as a fraction of it. Scatters the magnitude, not the direction - a branch does not flip sides

fields.label: Flower Count
fields.description: Flowers per inflorescence. Ignored by Solitary and by the cymose kinds, which get their count from how many times they relay instead - that is Branching Depth times Relays per Node

fields.label: Flowers per Whorl
fields.description:
How many flowers each node of the inflorescence carries, in a ring around the stem. 0 follows the plant's own leaf arrangement, which is one flower per leaf position - so 0 is exactly what every kind did before this existed.

Separate from Trunk Pattern on purpose: one flower is placed per leaf position, so asking for a six-flowered whorl through the phyllotaxis also gives the leafy stem below six leaves per node. A mint has two. This is the flowering region stating its own arrangement

fields.label: Flower Count Variance
fields.description: Random change to how many flowers each inflorescence carries, as a fraction of the count. Drawn once per stem, not per flower, so on a branched plant this is what stops every raceme being exactly the same length

fields.label: Pedicel Length
fields.description: Length of the pedicel - the little stalk between the stem and each flower. A corymb lengthens the lower ones automatically; a spike and a catkin ignore this, because their flowers are sessile and have no pedicel at all

fields.label: Pedicel Length Variance
fields.description: Random length on each pedicel, as a fraction of its own length

fields.label: Pedicel Angle

endpoints.look: pedicel pressed flat down against the stem
pedicel straight out sideways, horizontal (default is +30, a little upswept)
pedicel pressed flat up against the stem toward the tip

fields.description: How far a pedicel tilts off horizontal. 0 leaves the stem straight out sideways, positive swings it up toward the tip, negative hangs it down for a drooping raceme. Plus or minus 90 presses it flat against the stem

fields.label: Head Spread
fields.description: How wide an umbel opens. Flowers fill the whole dome including its centre, not just its rim.

endpoints.look: a tight, nearly parallel cone of flowers
a flat hemisphere (a classic umbel)
a complete sphere of flowers: an Allium globe or an ivy head

fields.label: Head Radius
fields.description: How wide a flat-topped head is. The flowers pack evenly inside it, so this is what keeps a corymb or flat umbel compact instead of a wide sparse fan. Only used by Corymb and Flat Umbel

fields.label: Head Dome
fields.description: How far the outer flowers of a flat-topped head sit below (or above) the middle ones, as a fraction of Head Radius. The curve beside it is the head's own cross-section from centre to rim. Only Corymb and Flat Umbel.

endpoints.look: the rim rises a full radius above the centre: a cupped bowl
dead flat (a true flat-top corymb)
the rim drops a full radius below the centre: a rounded mound as tall as it is wide

fields.label: Head Dome Variance
fields.description: Random height on each flower of a flat-topped head, as a fraction of Head Radius. Measured against the head rather than against Dome, so it roughens a flat top as readily as a domed one - which is where an even surface reads most artificial

fields.label: Pedicel Width

endpoints.look: hair-fine pedicels
conspicuously finer than the stem (default), as most plants carry them
as thick as the stem itself: reads as a short branch, not a flower stalk

fields.description: How thick each pedicel is where it leaves the stem, as a fraction of the stem's own thickness there. 1 continues the stem's width, which reads as a short branch; most plants carry conspicuously finer pedicels than that

fields.label: Pedicel Bend
fields.description: How strongly each pedicel curves along its length. This is SHAPE only and does NOT move the flower -- the pedicel arcs between the same two endpoints, so Length and Angle still decide where the flower sits.

endpoints.look: straight spokes
leaves the stem sideways and turns up on its way to the flower, the way a corymb does (default)
a strong curve (never wider than the flower's own reach)

fields.label: Flower Spacing

endpoints.look: flowers packed almost on top of each other: a dense spike or head
the flowering region tighter than the leafy stem below it (default)
flowers spaced further apart than the stem's own leaves: a lax, open raceme

fields.description: Spacing between flowers along the axis, relative to the leafy stem's own internode length. Below 1 packs the flowering region tighter than the stem below it, which is how most inflorescences sit

fields.label: Bloom Order

acropetal.label: Bottom first
acropetal.desc: Lowest flowers open first and are furthest along

centripetal.label: Outside first
centripetal.desc: Outer flowers open first, working inward

centrifugal.label: Middle first
centrifugal.desc: Central flowers open first, working outward

fields.description: Which flowers open first. Later ones are still opening, so they read smaller and tighter

fields.label: Young Size
fields.description: How big an inflorescence is the moment it is laid down, as a share of mature - its flower spacing, flower size and pedicel length and width all start here and grow to full as it develops. Only the youngest racemes (started near the end of the season) show it; a mature one is always full size. The curve beside it shapes the growth from this start to full

fields.label: Spread

endpoints.look: every flower on a single line up one side (strongly secund)
flowers crowded onto a quarter of the stem's circumference (one-sided, like foxglove)
flowers over half the circumference
the full circle the leaf arrangement gives (default, all round the stem)

fields.description: How much of the stem's circumference the flowers occupy. 360 is the full circle the leaf arrangement already gives; narrow it to crowd them onto one side, the way a foxglove does, and 0 puts every flower on a single line

fields.label: Spread Variance
fields.description: Random scatter on each flower's own position round the stem, in degrees either way

fields.label: Flower Pitch
fields.description: Which way each flower faces, stated like Pedicel Angle and measured the same way. Separate from the pedicel's own angle, so a hanging flower and an outward one can share one pedicel shape. Set it equal to Pedicel Angle to point straight along the pedicel.

endpoints.look: flower nods straight down (a hanging bell, like foxglove)
flower faces straight out sideways (default)
flower faces straight up (like a buttercup held to the sky)

fields.label: Flower Pitch Variance
fields.description: Random tilt on each flower, in degrees either way

fields.label: Flower Size Variance
fields.description: Random size on each flower, as a fraction of its own size

fields.label: Pedicel Angle Variance
fields.description: Random tilt on each pedicel, in degrees either way

fields.label: Pedicel Bend Variance
fields.description: Random curvature on each pedicel, as a fraction of its own bend

fields.label: Pedicel Width Variance
fields.description: Random thickness on each pedicel, as a fraction of its own

fields.label: Flower Spacing Variance
fields.description: Random change to the gap between one flower and the next, as a fraction of it. Drawn per gap, so a single raceme's own flowers sit unevenly

fields.label: Attachment Location

terminal.label: Terminal
terminal.desc: Each stem finishes by becoming the inflorescence - the usual case, and what a foxglove, a yarrow or an allium does

axillary.label: Axillary
axillary.desc:
Inflorescences arise at nodes along the stems, each on its own short stalk, while the stems go on being stems and bear no flowers themselves. Wisteria, laburnum, birch and hazel.

The stalks are not branches: they carry no leaves and sit outside Branch Density and Branching Zone, so those keep describing the plant's woody shape. Pair with Orientation to make them hang

internodal.label: Internodal
internodal.desc: From partway along an internode rather than at a node. Uncommon, but real - and the position along the internode is settable below

leaf_opposed.label: Leaf-opposed
leaf_opposed.desc:
At a node, but on the far side of the stem from the leaf rather than in its axil - oppositifolious, as grapes and pepper are.

Half a turn round from where an axillary one would sit; everything else about it matches Axillary

cauliflorous.label: Cauliflorous
cauliflorous.desc:
Straight out of wood laid down seasons earlier on the TRUNK, well below the leaves - cauliflory, as figs and cacao do.

Defined by age rather than position: nothing appears until a node has carried for the stated number of steps, so a young plant shows none

ramiflorous.label: Ramiflorous
ramiflorous.desc:
The same old-wood break as Cauliflorous, but along the BRANCHES instead of the trunk - ramiflory, as redbud does on bare limbs.

Shares the Wood Age gate; the two differ only in which stems may bear it

basal.label: Basal
basal.desc:
From the root crown, straight out of the ground rather than from anywhere up a stem - violets, many bulbs, and a primrose's scapes.

Arises at once rather than waiting on Wood Age: a basal scape is the first thing such a plant does

adventitious.label: Adventitious
adventitious.desc:
From old wood that never carried a meristem at all - scattered between the nodes, following no phyllotaxis.

The one position whose buds are made rather than found, which is what makes it adventitious. Shares the Wood Age gate; use Per Node to set how many break from each internode

fields.description: Where the inflorescences arise - at the tips of stems, along them, out of old wood, or from the base of the plant

fields.label: Wood Age
fields.description: How many growth steps a node must have carried before an inflorescence can break from it. Only used by From Old Wood - it is what makes cauliflory a matter of age rather than of position

fields.label: Per Node
fields.description:
How many inflorescences arise at each position the attachment picks - 1 is a single one, higher fans a cluster out from the same point.

This is what a 'terminal cluster' or an 'axillary cluster' is: a count applied to a position, not a position of its own. As one control it clusters any attachment, including ones a fixed pair of cluster entries could never have covered

fields.label: Along Internode
fields.description: Where along the internode it sits, 0 at the node below and 1 at the node above. Only used by Between Nodes

fields.label: Start
fields.description: How far up a stem they begin, 0 at its base and 1 at its tip

fields.label: End
fields.description: How far up a stem they stop

fields.label: Slide
fields.description: SPECIES: shifts the whole flowering/placement window up or down the stem without changing its width. Positive slides it toward the tip.

fields.label: On Trunk
fields.description: Whether the main stem bears inflorescences

fields.label: On Branches
fields.description: Whether side branches bear them. Hazel and birch carry theirs near the tips of the previous year's side twigs, which is what the default says

fields.label: Orientation

parent_aligned.label: Parent-aligned
parent_aligned.desc:
Prefer to lie along the stem that carries it, whatever that stem is doing.

Re-read as the plant grows, so the inflorescence swings when the branch bends. At Strength 0 this is simply the angle it left the stem at, which is what every plant did before orientation existed

erect.label: Erect
erect.desc: Prefer to point up, against gravity

horizontal.label: Horizontal
horizontal.desc:
Prefer to lie level, perpendicular to gravity.

Level is a whole plane, so it keeps the compass direction the bud already had - radially out from its own stem - rather than sending every inflorescence to one side of the plant

custom.label: Custom
custom.desc: Prefer the angle set below, measured from the parent stem's own direction rather than from world vertical - so it is stated relative to the stem and swings with it

fields.description: Which direction this inflorescence prefers to point

fields.label: Strength

endpoints.look: keeps exactly the direction it grew at; the mode's preference is ignored
pulled halfway toward the preferred direction, over a gentle arc
pulled fully onto the preference (though weight still bends it further); the arc onto it is at its sharpest

fields.description:
How far the inflorescence is pulled from the direction it would naturally leave the stem at, toward the preferred direction above.

0 leaves it exactly as it grew; 1 pulls it fully onto the preference. It is a preference rather than a rule - even at 1 the result keeps some of where it came from, and the stem's own weight then bends it further, so an organ is not forced onto exact vertical.

It also sets how sharply the turn happens: the turn is always spread over the same short run of nodes, so a bigger pull bends harder over that run. Higher is sharper, and no value gives a hard corner

fields.label: Angle

endpoints.look: continues straight along the parent stem's heading
held perpendicular to the parent stem
doubled fully back on the parent (straight down if the parent points up): a pendent chain

fields.description:
Custom's angle, measured from the parent stem's own direction. 0 continues straight along the stem, positive tips away from vertical, negative back toward it.

Only used by Custom - the other four state their own direction

fields.label: Reach It As Flowers Open
fields.description:
Arrive at the preferred direction as the inflorescence fills with flowers, rather than over its first few nodes - upright while it is a bud, bowed over once laden.

Different from Droop, which bends the finished stem: this moves while the inflorescence is still growing, so it changes where the flowers are actually placed

fields.label: Topology Override
fields.description: SPECIES/advanced: forces a specific structural topology regardless of the chosen Kind (blank = derive it from the Kind, which is almost always right). Used only when a species needs a form the Kind name cannot state. Copy from a preset rather than setting by hand.

fields.label: Apex
fields.description: SPECIES/advanced (the vegetativeness model): how floral the growing apex is. Leave veg unset: a tip then flowers exactly when the inflorescence is Terminal, and flowers along the stems come from its Axillary / Internodal / Leaf-opposed attachments. Copy veg.* from a preset only for forms the attachments cannot express (e.g. a true panicle vs a cyme).

fields.label: Lateral Offset
fields.description: SPECIES/advanced: how floral the lateral buds are RELATIVE to the apex. Opposite sign to the apex gives the determinate/indeterminate contrast that produces the different inflorescence forms. Copy from a preset.

fields.label: Decline
fields.description: SPECIES/advanced: how fast a meristem loses vegetativeness as the plant ages -- the rate of the floral transition. Copy from a preset.

fields.label: Threshold
fields.description: SPECIES/advanced: the vegetativeness level at which a meristem switches to making flowers. Copy from a preset.

fields.label: Catkin Length

endpoints.look: no catkins at all
a hazel-length hanging catkin
a long birch/willow-length catkin

fields.description:
How long each catkin is. 0 means none.

A catkin is built as a hanging curve rather than placed as a model, so it sags under its own weight, keeps the length you give it, and bends when the branch carrying it moves. It hangs from a node on its own stalk - it is not the tip of the branch

fields.label: Catkin Length Variance
fields.description: Length scatter between catkins. Drawn per catkin rather than per stalk, so the ones sharing a stalk differ from each other and not just from the next stalk's. Real catkins on one twig are visibly unequal

fields.label: Catkins per Stalk
fields.description:
How many catkins hang from one stalk. Hazel, birch and willow all carry them in small bunches rather than singly.

Separate from the leaf arrangement above, deliberately: how many catkins share a stalk and how the foliage is arranged are independent, and a whorled arrangement used to be the only way to get bunches - which whorled the leaves too

fields.label: Catkins per Stalk Variance
fields.description: Scatter in how many catkins each stalk carries. Hazel's bunches run two to four, and a plant whose every stalk carries exactly three reads as instanced

fields.label: Catkin Width

endpoints.look: a thread-thin catkin
a typical fat hazel catkin (default)
a very stout catkin body

fields.description: How thick the catkin body is at its fattest. It swells from nothing at the stalk to this in the middle and closes again at the tip, which is what gives it rounded ends rather than a tube cut off flat

fields.label: Catkin Density
fields.description: SPECIES/mesh: how many rings are swept along a catkin's length -- its mesh resolution, not a shape control. Raise only if a long catkin looks faceted.

fields.label: Catkin Stalk Variance
fields.description: Length scatter between one stalk and the next, so the bunches sit at different distances from the twig. Separate from Length's own variance, which scatters the catkins on a stalk rather than the stalks themselves

fields.label: Catkin Stalk
fields.description: The bare stalk between the node and the start of the catkin body. This is what makes a catkin read as hanging off a twig rather than sprouting from it

fields.label: Catkin Hang Variance
fields.description: Random scatter in how far each catkin hangs, around the Orientation angle above. A per-catkin variance, which an angle stated for a whole inflorescence has no equivalent of

fields.label: Catkin Noise
fields.description: Bends each catkin slightly out of true, so a bunch does not read as several copies of one tube. Subtle by design - it bends the whole shape gently rather than roughening the surface, and grows from nothing where the catkin attaches to full at its free end

fields.label: Spacing Base

endpoints.look: very short internodes: a congested, rosette-like or cushion stem
an ordinary perennial spacing (default)
long bare internodes; combined with Whorled + Branches Per Node this is what tiers a monkey-puzzle (Araucaria)

fields.description: The inflorescence's spacing base: the distance between flowers is this times Flower Spacing (Branch Spacing on a branched rachis), the same on every stem and branch. Stem and branch internodes are the Branching levels' Length instead

fields.label: Leaf Angle

endpoints.look: leaf pressed up flat against the stem (appressed, erect)
a typical ascending leaf
leaf straight out horizontal (spreading)

fields.description: Angle a leaf leaves the stem at, measured from the stem

fields.label: Leaf Size
fields.description: Multiplier on the leaf mesh's own size (1.0 = the mesh exactly as the user modelled it). Set relative proportions, not absolute size. Young leaves near a growing tip expand up from small automatically. Leaf mass scales with the SQUARE of this, so a bigger leaf also weighs more and droops its own stem a little further.

fields.label: Variation
fields.description: How much leaf size varies leaf to leaf

fields.label: Yaw
fields.description: Swings each leaf left or right within its own plane, without tilting it -- the blade stays as flat as it was and simply no longer points straight out from the stem.

endpoints.look: swung fully back toward the stem base on one side
points straight out from the stem
swung fully back on the other side

fields.label: Yaw Variation
fields.description: How far individual leaves swing either side of the Yaw angle. Real leaves are not all turned the same way, and a few degrees of scatter is what separates a grown plant from a modelled one

fields.label: Roll
fields.description: Rotates each leaf about its own midrib, so its face stops being flat to the sky without the blade pointing anywhere new.

endpoints.look: rolled fully over, underside up
face flat to the sky
blade turned on edge

fields.label: Roll Variation
fields.description: How far individual leaves roll either side of the Roll angle

fields.label: Flower Size
fields.description: Multiplier on the flower mesh's own size (1.0 = the mesh as modelled). This is the single flower-size control: the flower_size_profile curve grades it along the inflorescence and each flower's bloom-opening is folded in on top. Flower mass scales with the CUBE of this, so doubling a head's size makes it eight times heavier -- size and weight together decide how far a blooming tip nods.

fields.label: Fruit Size
fields.description: Size of each ripe fruit, a multiplier on the fruit asset mesh (mesh-driven, like Flower Size). A fruit is its own organ at its own size, not the flower it set from. Effective mass grows with the CUBE of Fruit Size, so a big fruit bows the branch far harder.

fields.label: Gravitropism

endpoints.look: no correction at all: the tip keeps whatever heading Growth Irregularity gives it, so the stem meanders and a tall one flops over
gently self-righting: a natural, slightly wavy upright stem (the default herbaceous look)
snaps back to and holds its target heading every step: a stiff, rigidly erect stem

fields.description: How strongly a stem corrects back toward the angle it is trying to hold. Higher makes stems stiff and true; lower lets them wander

fields.label: Circumnutation
fields.description: The coherent, helical counterpart to Growth Irregularity: instead of wandering at random each step, the tip nods around a rotating azimuth, so it winds a tight spiral rather than sprawling -- the endogenous spiralling seen in growth timelapses. Measured, at the same per-step bend size an incoherent wander drifts ~68 mm off a 1.2 m stem while this coherent one stays a ~13 mm helix. Its amplitude is fought by Gravitropism, so on a stiff upright stem the nod is straightened almost as fast as it is made and reads faintly; lower Gravitropism, or raise Autotropism to keep the nod at the growing tip.

endpoints.look: off: no helical nod (byte-identical to a plant without it)
a gentle coherent spiral; a clear corkscrew at low Gravitropism, a faint helical waviness at the default
a pronounced winding stem, over-coiled and floppy at low Gravitropism

fields.label: Circumnutation Rate
fields.description: How far the nod turns around the stem each step -- the pitch of the helix. Its sign is the handedness (positive winds one way, negative the other). Does nothing while Circumnutation is 0.

endpoints.look: the golden angle: a tight, natural spiral (default)
a long, stretched helix -- few gentle turns up the stem
the same tight spiral wound the other way

fields.label: Autotropism
fields.description: Age-stiffening: older stem straightens back toward its own gravitropic setpoint as it ages, applied once after growth. It leaves a mature stem tidy while the growing tip still nods -- the canonical 'straight stem, live circumnutating tip' of a timelapse. It only ever undoes wander, never adds it, and is a separate pass from Droop, which sags the finished stem down under load. With no Circumnutation it simply tidies the random Growth Irregularity of older stem.

endpoints.look: off: the stem keeps its full wander/nod all the way down (a uniform helix)
the lower stem straightens to true; the nod is confined to the top several nodes
aggressive: only the top few nodes still move, on an otherwise ruler-true stem

fields.label: Light Seeking

endpoints.look: ignores light direction; only gravity and the setpoint steer growth
tips lean strongly out from under whatever shades them each step (phototropic reaching)

fields.description: How far growing tips turn toward the light each step. Applied after Gravitropism, so a shaded shoot leans out from under whatever is shading it even though gravity would hold it upright. 0 ignores light direction

fields.label: Flower Heliotropism
fields.description: How far each flower turns its face toward the sun, as a post-growth re-aim that leaves the flower where it is -- the nodding-sunflower case: the stalk hangs where gravity left it, the head still turns to the sun. The sun is any object you pick for the plant to track (its Sun Object): flowers face wherever it sits relative to the plant, so move it to place the sun. No object picked, no effect; this strength is the species trait. Distinct from light_seeking, which turns growing shoots toward a light gradient rather than re-aiming the organs on them.

endpoints.look: off: flowers face wherever their stalk and pitch aimed them
each flower turns halfway from its grown facing toward the sun
every flower faces the sun exactly, however its stalk hangs

fields.label: Leaf Heliotropism
fields.description: How far each leaf turns its blade to face the sun (diaheliotropic, the light-gathering pose), a post-growth re-aim like flower_heliotropism and sharing the same tracked Sun Object. Its own strength because a species may track one organ and not the other. Distinct from an ALIGN effector, which twists the whole growth frame -- rotating the leaf set and the branches with it -- rather than pointing each blade at the sun; ALIGN barely moves aggregate sun-facing on a spiral phyllotaxis, where this points every blade at the sun.

endpoints.look: off: leaves lie however they grew
blades turn halfway toward facing the sun
every blade's broad face points at the sun

fields.label: Clearance

endpoints.look: obstacle response off entirely; tips ignore surfaces
tips curve away well before a surface and stop rather than grow through it

fields.description: How far from a surface this plant keeps its growing tips. Tips curve away as they approach, and one that runs out of room stops there instead of growing through. 0 turns obstacle response off entirely

fields.label: Emergence Day
fields.description: Day of the year the plant emerges and its growing season starts (around 90 = spring). Shifts where the whole life sits on the calendar. Moves into the calendar widget later

fields.label: Season Length
fields.description: Length of the growing season in days, emergence to full maturity. Longer spreads the same growth over more real days. Moves into the calendar widget later

fields.label: Lifespan

null.label: Single season
null.desc: One season that stays mature past its end -- the original behaviour. Nothing changes when the Day is scrubbed into a later year

annual.label: Annual
annual.desc: Lives one season, then dies at season end (fully senesced, standing) and never comes back

herbaceous_perennial.label: Herbaceous perennial
herbaceous_perennial.desc: Dies back to bare ground each winter and regrows a fresh top each spring, a touch bigger year over year to a mature plateau

fields.description: How the plant lives across years. Only affects Days scrubbed past the first season -- the mature Day-270 view is the same for all three

fields.label: Plastochron
fields.description: SPECIES timing: how many developmental steps pass between one node appearing and the next. 1 lays a node every step.

fields.label: Elongation Duration
fields.description: SPECIES timing: how many steps a freshly made internode takes to stretch from nothing to full length.

fields.label: Leaf Expansion Duration
fields.description: SPECIES timing: how many steps a new leaf takes to expand from a small primordium to full size. This is the maturity cue that keeps young leaves near a tip small.

fields.label: Droop
fields.description: How far the whole grown plant sags under its own weight, applied AFTER growth (it bends the finished structure, it does not change what is attached to what -- that is Gravitropism). Resisted by Stem Stiffness; driven by the organ weights. A heavier flower nods its own stem further.

endpoints.look: rigid: the plant holds exactly the shape it grew
a gentle, natural sag (default)
clearly weeping tips and outer branches
folds over heavily under its own mass

fields.label: Stem Stiffness
fields.description: How strongly stems resist bending, as an elastic modulus (the number stored in the preset). Because thick parts already resist far more than thin ones (resistance goes as radius to the fourth power), raising this mostly straightens the tips and outer branches while the base barely moves. Low (~1e7) is limp and herbaceous; the default 1.5e8 is a firm green stem; high (~1e9+) is woody and stiff.

endpoints.look: limp, floppy stems
a firm herbaceous stem (default)
woody, stiff; only the thinnest tips give at all

fields.label: Stiffness Profile
fields.description: How stem stiffness varies along an axis, base to tip, as a multiplier on Stem Stiffness. Stiffer at the base and softer toward the tip, a woody base under a green tip, lets a plant hold itself up while its tips still nod; flat treats the whole stem as one material. Because bending resistance goes as the fourth power of radius, the taper already does most of this, so the curve is a finer adjustment on top of it.

fields.label: Stiffness Variance
fields.description: Random stem-to-stem variation in stiffness across a clump, as a fraction. Drawn once per stem, so a stand of the same plant bends differently one to the next without any single stem becoming ragged along its own length

fields.label: Rigid Base
fields.description: What fraction of each stem, measured from the ground up, stays stiff and unbending -- so the bend is concentrated above it, the way a lignified (woody) base carries a softer flowering tip. This only MOVES the bend, it does not reduce it: the same curvature is packed into a shorter stretch, so Droop and the organ weights still decide how far it goes.

endpoints.look: the whole stem may curve: a plant folding over from the ground
the lower half holds firm, the upper half carries the bend
the lower 90% stays stiff and erect, so a heavy head nods only at the very top, like a poppy on its stalk
a stiff, erect stalk that gives only at its very tip

fields.label: Peduncle Droop
fields.description: How far the stretch of stem carrying the flowers turns over, on TOP of Droop -- stated as an angle, so it means the same on every plant whatever the flowers weigh. Raising it lengthens the drooping arc rather than tightening it: the flower swings further out and down at one steady radius. Where along the stem it happens is Rigid Base; how far below the lowest flower it may reach is Peduncle Reach.

endpoints.look: the flowering stretch holds the heading it grew (no extra nod)
turned ~45 degrees over
brought to horizontal (~90 degrees over): a nodding head
past horizontal, ~135 degrees, clearly hanging
hangs straight down (~180 degrees): a fully pendent spike or head

fields.label: Peduncle Reach
fields.description: How far below the lowest flower the drooping stretch extends, as real stem length in metres. This SPREADS the turn, it does not add to it: at 0 the whole bend lands on one node and hooks sharply; longer values curve it over more stem to the same final angle. A solitary flower sits on the very tip, so it needs some of this just to have a stalk to bend.

endpoints.look: a sharp one-node hook right under the flower
the bend spread over a short arch
a long gentle sweep down a good length of stem

fields.label: Bend Resolution

endpoints.look: no extra segments: on a short drooping stretch a big turn reads as two hard facets (default)
each internode in the bending stretch split in four: a smooth curve
very smooth; only needed where a large droop lands on very few nodes

fields.description:
How many segments each internode in a hard-bending stretch is split into. A bend can only be as smooth as the stem is dense, and on a solitary flower the drooping stretch is a couple of nodes at the very top - so a big turn across them reads as two sharp facets rather than a curve.

Two stretches get it: the drooping region below the lowest flower, and the whole of every inflorescence BRANCH - a compound umbel's ray is only a couple of nodes long and is bent by its own Bend, its Droop and the plant's, all landing on the same one or two joints.

The rest of the plant is untouched. 1 changes nothing

fields.label: Senescence Onset
fields.description: When a branch becomes eligible to die back, over the plant's life. Only matters when a senescence trigger is on (Shade Threshold, or age dieback): it holds the plant whole early and lets the oldest, most-shaded parts drop as it matures.

fields.label: Keep Dead Wood
fields.description: Whether a dead branch stays as grey dead wood, or is removed entirely. Its leaves and flowers are shed either way -- a dead branch is bare

fields.label: Shade Death

endpoints.look: nothing ever dies of shade (default)
branches in moderate shade die back, taking their subtree with them: a lifted, bare lower crown
anything not in full sky dies: only the outermost lit shell of the plant survives

fields.description: After growth, each branch is judged by the light at its base; below this it dies and takes its subtree with it. 0 (default) never kills. The plant shades itself, so this works with no obstacle in the scene; add obstacles overhead to shade a lower crown. 1.0 kills anything out of full sky

fields.label: Wood Density
fields.description: SPECIES / physics: the stem tissue's mass per unit volume, in kg/m3. It feeds the self-weight that Droop bends, so denser wood sags more for the same stiffness. Real references: balsa about 150; softwoods (pine, spruce, fir) about 350 to 450; medium hardwoods (birch, cherry) about 600 to 650; dense hardwoods (oak about 700, beech 720, maple 750); and the hardest (ebony, lignum vitae) over 1000. The default 500 sits between a softwood and a light hardwood; a green herbaceous stem behaves like the low end, seasoned hardwood the high end.

fields.label: Leaf Weight
fields.description: How heavy a full-size leaf is, on the same relative scale as Flower Weight. Leaf mass is small against stem stiffness on most plants, so this reads far more subtly than the flower's. Effective mass scales with the square of Leaf Size.

fields.label: Flower Weight
fields.description: How heavy a full-size flower or head is, on a relative scale. This is the main thing that nods a blooming tip: a heavy head on a thin stem hangs, a light one stands up. Effective mass grows with the CUBE of Flower Size, so size and weight together decide the droop.

fields.label: Fruit Weight
fields.description: How heavy a full-size ripe fruit is, on the same relative scale as Flower Weight but heavier -- what bows a fruiting branch. Fruit exists only inside the calendar fruit window, so the branch droops as fruit ripens and springs back after fruit-drop. Effective mass grows with the CUBE of Fruit Size.

fields.label: Fruit Set
fields.description: Fraction of flowers that set fruit, rolled per flower. The rest are unpollinated and drop at fruit-set. Only affects the day path, inside the calendar fruit window.

endpoints.look: every flower becomes a fruit
about half of the flowers set; the rest drop
no fruit sets

fields.label: Flowering Onset
fields.description: The gate on flowering over the plant's life: below the curve an axis cannot flower yet, whatever its node count. It opens flowering as the plant matures. Deliberately reaches 1 well before an axis finishes its nodes, so it is a permission gate rather than a bloom schedule; the moment an axis actually flowers is set structurally by Nodes Before Flowering.

fields.label: Leaf Size Profile
fields.description: Leaf size along the stem, base to tip, as a multiplier on Leaf Size. Larger at the base is the common case, big basal leaves giving way to smaller ones up the stem; a rosette species drops it hard just above the base.

fields.label: Leaf Angle Profile
fields.description: How a leaf's angle varies up the stem, base to tip, as a multiplier on Leaf Angle. Opening the base, so lower leaves sit more horizontal and upper ones more erect, reads as a plant presenting its lower leaves to the light.

fields.label: Elongation
fields.description: How a freshly made internode stretches from nothing to full length over its Elongation Steps: the horizontal axis is that internode's own growth time, not position on the plant. A gentle ease-out reads as natural extension, a straight ramp as mechanical. This is why a young tip's internodes are still short, they have not finished elongating.

fields.label: Leaf Expansion
fields.description: How a new leaf expands from a tiny primordium to full size over its Leaf Expansion Steps: the horizontal axis is the leaf's own growth time. It is the maturity cue that keeps leaves near a growing tip small while older leaves lower down are full-sized, all on the one Age dial.
